extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning and natural language understanding, focusing on everyday situations with a preference for atypical solutions.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com and asked to articulate a physical goal and a valid solution. They were also asked to provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid (a trick). Data was collected in batches and validated by other annotators.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was cleaned of basic stylistic artifacts and trivial examples using the AFLite algorithm, which performs systematic data bias reduction by discarding instances whose feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was tokenized by Spacy. For model experiments, examples were truncated at 150 tokens.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were seeded with instructables drawn from six categories (costume, outside, craft, home, food, and workshop) to inspire them to construct two component tasks. They articulated a goal and a valid solution, and then provided a subtle permutation to render the solution incorrect. A diff button highlighted where solutions differed. A qualification HIT was used, and data was validated by other annotators for correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Data was validated by other annotators for correctness. Examples with low agreement were removed from the data, which often included correct examples requiring expert-level knowledge. Users with low agreement were de-qualed.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to elicit further research into building language representations that capture details of the real world, helping to build language tools which capture enough physical knowledge to speed up the bootstrapping of robotic-language applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors noted reporting bias where people are drawn to prototypical solutions and look for tools in the kitchen or garage. To address this and flatten the distribution of referenced objects, annotators were prompted with links to instructables. Stylistic artifacts were also removed using AFLite.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Correct examples requiring expert level knowledge of a domain (e.g., special woodworking terminology) were removed during validation, as they do not fall under 'commonsense'.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding and evaluating language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense via multiple choice question answering.
